title: Conserved Verdicts, Drifting Commitments: Identifying Harmful Overthinking
abstract: arXiv:2611.21946v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A reasoning model that has reached a correct answer can lose it by continuing to think. Deciding whether to stop means comparing two probabilities at the same point of a chain: that the answer the model would give if stopped now is correct (its commitment), and that the answer it will finish with is correct (its verdict). We show that the verdict alone, which is what final-correctness probes estimate, cannot make this comparison. As a forecast of a fixed outcome it has no predictable drift, whether continuing helps or hurts. The commitment-verdict gap equals the expected remaining change in answer quality and the accuracy gained by stopping. A second identity splits any accuracy-versus-budget curve into answer change within chains and change in which chains are still running. We measure both on MATH-500. translated_title: 守恒的判定，漂移的承诺：识别有害的过度思考
translated_abstract: 一个已经得出正确答案的推理模型，可能会因为继续思考而失去这个正确答案。决定是否停止，意味着在推理链的同一位置比较两个概率：模型若现在停止所给出的答案是正确的概率（即其“承诺”），以及模型最终完成时的答案是正确的概率（即其“判定”）。我们证明，仅凭判定——也就是最终正确性探针所估计的量——无法完成这种比较。作为对一个固定结果的预测，判定没有可预测的漂移，无论继续思考是有益还是有害。承诺与判定之差等于答案质量的期望剩余变化量，也正是停止思考所能获得的准确率增益。第二个恒等式则将任何准确率-预算曲线分解为两部分：推理链内部的答案变化，以及仍在运行的推理链集合的变化。我们在 MATH-500 上对这两者进行了测量。在 DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B 持有正确答案的全部 379 个点上（这些点的选取不考虑其推理链如何结束），继续……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该论文提出“承诺-判定差距”框架来识别推理模型中的有害过度思考，证明仅凭最终正确性探针估计的“判定”无法预测继续思考的利弊，而“承诺”与“判定”之差恰好量化了停止思考可获得的准确率增益，并给出将准确率-预算曲线分解为链内答案变化与链存活变化的恒等式。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the commitment-verdict gap to identify harmful overthinking in reasoning models, showing that verdict-only final-correctness probes cannot predict whether continued reasoning helps or hurts, while the gap quantifies the accuracy gained by stopping and decomposes any accuracy-versus-budget curve into within-chain answer changes and changes in which chains remain active.
